messages:
pager-duty-bot: PAGER: P1 - routing-service (router-proxy) in eu-west-1: 5xx rate > 8% over 60s. Pager: @oncall. Incident channel created.

Sara L.: I'm on it, grabbing logs now. Anyone oncall already?

Mike R.: I'm the primary oncall for infra. Jumping in. Sara, can you confirm customer impact?

Sara L.: Dashboards show ~12% error rate on /route endpoint for eu-west-1. Latency for succeeded requests up ~120ms but main issue is the 5xx spike. Affected customers: multiple; top visible is AcmeCorp (spike in error budget alerts).

Jin T.: I see a correlated spike in routed-to-variant mismatches in the routing logs (router-proxy). Example trace id: trace=3fa2b8a4. Getting sample logs now.

Sara L.: Pasting sample from router-proxy stdout:
```
2026-06-07T14:12:05Z router-proxy [info] request_id=3fa2b8a4 customer=acmecorp route_rule=eu-west-1 tier=prod target_model=redwood-v2 fallback_model=rw-lite mismatch=true err="model_compatibility: weight vector mismatch" status=502
```

Mike R.: That mismatch=true line is interesting. We had the policy change last night to enable model fallback across tiers (to reduce drops) — maybe fallback selection is returning incompatible variants.

Dmitri P.: I can confirm the config push: `routing-policies: allow_fallback=true cross_tier=true` deployed 03:40 UTC. Rolling back to previous policy would stop cross-tier fallbacks.

Eva K.: If fallback is returning a quantized-only model for requests that expect full-precision KV cache behaviour, that would trigger runtime errors (502) in the serving runtime. We saw a similar pattern in staging last month.

Sara L.: What do traces show for the sequence pre-failure? Full trace dump for 3fa2b8a4: router -> model-selector -> assignment: candidate=rw-lite-q4 -> assign -> serve -> runtime error: `kv_cache_missing_for_sequence` -> 502.

Mike R.: Immediate mitigation: disable cross-tier fallback in routing policy or force fallback to same-compatibility family. I'll revert the config. Rolling revert now.

Infra Bot: config-push: routing-policy-service reverted to `allow_fallback=false` by user mike.r at 14:16:22 UTC.

Sara L.: After revert, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.1% in eu-west-1 within 90s. Latency normalizing. :thumbsup:

Jin T.: Confirmed. New traces show consistent candidate selection: candidate=redwood-v2 (compatible). No more `kv_cache_missing` errors in recent logs.

Dmitri P.: Logging extract:
```
14:16:01 router-proxy request_id=abc123 assigned=redwood-v2 status=200
14:16:02 router-proxy request_id=def456 assigned=redwood-v2 status=200
```

Eva K.: Quick customer note: AcmeCorp saw retries from their side earlier and may have rate-limited their downstream callers. We should notify any customers with elevated error budgets.

Sara L.: I'll open a customer-impact thread and ping CSMs.

Mike R.: Root cause hypothesis: config change allowed cross-tier fallbacks; the fallback selector sometimes chose a quantized-only variant (rw-lite-q4) incompatible with the request's expected cache/kv behavior, causing runtime to respond with 502. The policy change reduced availability in some edge cases.

Jin T.: Supporting evidence: (1) timestamps align with config push, (2) trace IDs show `kv_cache_missing_for_sequence`, (3) reverting policy reduced 5xx.

Dmitri P.: Secondary hypothesis: under load, model-selector's compatibility scoring degraded due to a bug in the compatibility matrix lookup (edge-case null pointer) causing it to default to first candidate which was q4. Need to check selector logs for nulls.

Eva K.: Mitigation checklist for now: 1) keep `allow_fallback=false` (Mike has reverted) 2) add guard in model-selector to avoid assigning quantized-only variants to sequences requiring KV cache. 3) run compatibility validation suite against routing-policy changes in CI.

Mike R.: I'll keep revert in place until we ship a patch. Can we get a hotfix PR for a guard clause? Jin/Dmitri, can you pair on that?

Jin T.: Yes. I'll open a PR and tag @Dmitri. Include unit tests that simulate `sequence.requires_kv_cache=true` and candidate lists containing q4-only models.

Dmitri P.: On it. I'll also pull logs from the model-selector service for the 03:40–03:50 window to search for `null` entries.

Sara L.: I'll handle incident summary and customer notifications. Draft updates:
- Impact: Elevated 5xx (peak ~12%) for router-proxy in eu-west-1 affecting multiple customers including AcmeCorp.
- Trigger: routing-policy change enabling cross-tier fallback (deployed 03:40 UTC).
- Mitigation: reverted policy at 14:16:22 UTC; 5xx rate reduced to baseline within 2 minutes.
- Next steps: fix selector guard, CI compatibility test, postmortem + timeline.

Infra Bot: incident-note: postmortem requested. Owner assigned: Sara L.

Mike R.: Action items assigned: Mike (keep revert active + coordinate rollback window), Jin (PR for guard), Dmitri (logs + selector telemetry), Eva (customer comms). We'll do a follow-up bridge at 16:00 UTC to confirm patch and rollout plan.

Sara L.: Thanks all. Adding a timeline artifact to the incident doc with sample trace ids: 3fa2b8a4, abc123, def456.

Jin T.: PR link: https://git.redwood.internal/routing/model-selector/pulls/542 (draft). Includes unit tests and a runtime guard.

Dmitri P.: Found one selector log with unexpected null fields at 03:41:07 UTC, pushing extract to the incident doc.

Sara L.: Closing active mitigation notes. We'll keep monitoring eu-west-1 for 2 hours post-mitigation and update CSMs. Will post final RCA once root cause confirmed.

Mike R.: Good job. Marking as triaged.

pager-duty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Mike R. Channel quieting measures removed.
